main_body: A wooden pew drawn as a wide bench seen straight from the front: horizontal alternating dark and mid brown plank bands (backrest slats) with a lighter tan band in the lower middle, side posts at left and right.
top_band: none — the top rows 0-1 are dark brown, the same tone family as the slats below; no lighter horizontal surface is visible from above
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: dark brown (rows 0-1), mid brown plank (2-3), dark stripe (4-5), mid brown (6), light tan band (7-8), a mid-tone band with texture (9), another tan band (10-11), dark stripe (12-13). These are alternating horizontal slats, all vertical faces. No lighter, foreshortened seat surface is seen from above, and there are no legs or seat depth. It reads as a front elevation of a bench back and fails the 'seat surface must be seen from above' requirement.

style.evidence: The pew has about 4 brown steps (dark, mid, light tan, mid highlight), with dark-brown side posts that are tinted wood tones rather than black. Texture is limited to a few speckles in the lower tan band; the mid-brown slats are large flat fills. Compared with the stall and well references, which carry many tones, tile-by-tile detail and grain, the pew is much sparser per tile and reads flatter.
